summary: Proxy auth token refresh strips version-pin header, causing mixed-model streaming responses
description:
Issue summary:
Customer KiteAnalytics reported intermittent mixed-model content inside long streaming responses for a pinned route. A single user stream would start returning tokens from the pinned version (growth-3b-v2) and midway through switch to the canary model (legacy-chat-7b) without an explicit fallback event in the application logs.

Impact:
- A small subset of long-running streaming sessions (approx 0.4% of requests during a 48h window) experienced content shifts mid-stream.
- Customer reported degraded coherence for long conversations and logged 14 high-priority support tickets internally.
- Affects production traffic in us-east-1 on dedicated capacity for KiteAnalytics.

Environment:
- prod us-east-1, Dedicated pool DK-11 serving growth-3b-v2 pinned routes.
- Fronted by API Gateway -> auth-proxy (session refresh service) -> streaming-router -> serving-runtime.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long streaming generate call with a pinned model version header (x-redwood-pin: growth-3b-v2).
2) Keep the connection open for >90s and generate multiple user messages (long conversation).
3) Trigger an auth token refresh (simulated by expiring session token) from the client side or wait for automatic refresh.
4) Observe that subsequent tokens in the same stream are produced by the canary model.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Router traces show initial route decision honored the x-redwood-pin header.
- At ~token N+48, logs show a header rewrite event at auth-proxy: Authorization header rotated and x-redwood-pin header absent in the rewritten request forwarded to streaming-router.
- Serving-runtime accepted the request and routed to canary because pin metadata was missing.
- No explicit fallback policy triggered in control-plane; router treated request as unpinned.
- Customer-provided transcript attached in comments (sensitive content redacted).

Hypothesis and root cause (investigation notes):
- The auth-proxy's session refresh path performs a conservative header sanitization pass when it swaps tokens; the code path intentionally removed unknown custom headers and reattached only whitelisted headers. x-redwood-pin was not on the whitelist and was dropped.
- Long-lived streaming requests that caused token refresh mid-stream got their pin metadata silently stripped, so routing fell back to default canary behavior.
- Short requests and non-streaming routes rarely hit the problematic path because token refresh happened client-side before request initiation.

Temporary mitigation / customer workaround:
- Immediately applied a proxy-side rule to preserve x-redwood-pin and x-redwood-session-id for streaming endpoints (hotfix ACL).
- Instructed KiteAnalytics to avoid client-side token expiry during a stream as a short-term workaround.
- Enabled request-level logging for affected customer routes to detect any further pin loss.

Permanent fix / next steps:
- Engineering (proxy team) to add x-redwood-pin and other inference routing headers to the proxy whitelist and add unit tests to prevent regression (PR opened: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/7241).
- Add integration test that simulates session refresh mid-stream and asserts pin preservation.
- Update runbook: streaming pin preservation and include checks in canary health verification.
- Roll out proxy hotfix to all regions; verify with synthetic streaming tests.

Status and timeline:
- Hotfix deployed to us-east-1 (mar 11) and confirmed to stop new occurrences for KiteAnalytics.
- Full rollout to eu-west and ap-southeast scheduled for mar 15 after automated test pass.

Resolution notes (work in progress):
- Auth-proxy whitelist adjusted in staging and prod us-east-1.
- Integration tests added to CI.
- Postmortem to follow once cross-region rollout completes.

Attachments: customer transcript excerpts, router trace snippets, auth-proxy logs (redacted).
